question: Drug used in cancer chemotherapy induced vomiting is?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Aprepitant" -> "NK1 receptor antagonist" -> "blocks substance P" -> "prevents vomiting" -> 90%
CHAIN: "All of the above" -> "Aprepitant, Dexamethasone, Ondansetron" -> "different mechanisms" -> "complementary antiemetic effects" -> 95%
analysis: In the context of cancer chemotherapy-induced vomiting, several classes of antiemetic drugs are used. Aprepitant is a neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor antagonist, dexamethasone is a corticosteroid, and ondansetron is a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist. All three are commonly used in combination to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV). Therefore, the most comprehensive answer is 'All of the above', as each drug plays a role in managing CINV.
